central_argument: Preserve tail-class abilities acquired during federated adaptation through source-aware historical margin targets; use client feedback to learn a supplementary combination of existing updates.

sections.role: State client-distribution-dependent retention problem; connect it to A and B
Locate the work among federated long-tail learning, visual adaptation and functional retention
Same-pool and fixed-marginal comparisons motivate retention; rank-2 diagnostic motivates response-based support
Derive source weights, current/historical targets, bounded correction and feedback-driven update combination
Report final configuration, paired component effects, sample retention and update reuse
Return to retaining acquired tail abilities and reusing client updates

budget_convention: Eight-page editorial budget includes figures and tables; Chinese working-copy layout is measured separately. References and supplementary material are outside the main-text budget. English translation requires its own layout check.
editorial_decisions: Joint is a disclosed fixed training configuration, not a contribution or separate main methodology section.
Final joint results and paired sample-weighted component experiments remain explicitly distinct.
No claims of generic SOTA, formal privacy, donor-pruning advantage or absent-label-only gain attribution.
Operational thresholds, solver settings and complete schedules are placed in the supplement.
No proposed multi-dataset experiment is represented as completed evidence.
